lead.t: A cardiovascular examination is incomplete without looking for evidence of heart failure and peripheral vascular disease.
lead.s: Approach to Cardiovascular Symptoms and Examination

b: Explain the examination, obtain consent, wash hands and position the patient appropriately. Expose the chest respectfully and examine the patient from the end of the bed before focusing on the precordium.
sec.s: Approach to Cardiovascular Symptoms and Examination

b: Assess heart sounds, murmurs, rhythm and signs of heart failure when indicated, especially where there is a history of cardiac disease, hypertension, breathlessness, syncope or reduced exercise tolerance.
sec.s: Preconception Care: A Practical Guide for MBChB Year 4

Bedside Cardiovascular Examination and Heart Murmurs

snip.t: Cardiovascular examination reveals a displaced apex beat, a new early diastolic murmur at the left sternal border, and splinter haemorrhages under the fingernails.

Examination: height, weight and BMI, blood pressure, pallor, oedema, breast and cardiovascular examination, abdominal examination (fundal height, lie, presentation, foetal heart), and a vaginal examination only when indicated.
